title: Partitioning vs clustering / indexing
summary: Theory / Data Modeling / Physical layout / Workload-led choices

children.text: How would you explain partitioning versus clustering or indexing to a teammate choosing storage for a large orders table?

items: Ask which database or table format is in use.
Identify selective predicates, common date ranges and write patterns.
Consider partition count, skew and small-file overhead.
Measure pruning, read volume and maintenance cost.

children.text: Partitioning divides data by a partition rule. Clustering often organizes nearby values within storage, while an index supplies an access structure. Exact meanings differ by engine. Start with filtering patterns and data distribution rather than assuming a universal layout.

children.title: Watch for this
children.text: A high-cardinality customer key is not automatically a good partition column. The word clustering does not promise identical behavior in every engine.

items: What would change if queries filter on dates but updates arrive for old customers?
Distinguish logical keys from physical layout.
Reason from workload rather than labels.
